sources.entry: Mounty - Tiny tool to re-mount write-protected NTFS volumes under Mac OS X 10.9+ in read-write mode. ![Freeware][Freeware Icon]

summary.name: Mounty
summary.one_liner: Mounty is a tiny macOS menu-bar tool that re-mounts write-protected NTFS volumes in read-write mode, using the NTFS-3G driver with macFUSE on macOS Ventura and later.
keywords: write to ntfs drive on mac
use_cases: Writing files to an NTFS-formatted external drive or USB stick on a Mac
Re-mounting an NTFS volume read-write after macOS mounts it read-only
Installing a free NTFS write driver on macOS via Homebrew
Accessing a Windows system partition from macOS (with caveats)
Recovering the state of a dirty NTFS volume by running chkdsk on Windows
summary.what_it_does: Mounty detects connected NTFS-formatted volumes and notifies the user when one is ready to re-mount in read-write mode. Since macOS Ventura it acts as a graphical front end for the open-source NTFS-3G driver, which requires macFUSE to be installed. Earlier macOS versions (10.9 to Monterey and some later) use the Apple kernel driver's hidden read-write mount function. A menu bar icon shows state (inactive, active, working, idle, error) and offers a Show in Finder option for the mounted drive. The page also lists an automount option and keychain storage for the mount password in some versions.
notable: Acts as a UI for the free NTFS-3G driver on macOS Ventura and later, with macFUSE as a dependency
Works with the Apple kernel driver on macOS 10.9 to Monterey, mounting NTFS read-write via a hidden option
Distributed free outside the Mac App Store because the App Store sandbox does not allow remounting external volumes
Installable with a single Homebrew cask command
caveats: Installation is more complex on macOS Ventura and later: macFUSE and ntfs-3g-mac must be installed and trusted in security settings, and a restart may be needed
Latest macOS 'Golden Gate' requires macFUSE at least 5.4.0
Mounting Windows system partitions can fail when Windows Fast Start or hibernation is enabled
Volumes not cleanly unmounted on Windows may be marked dirty and cannot be remounted read-write until repaired with chkdsk on Windows
